We need to implement solve(case) that takes a payload with word_token_indices (list of lists of ints), word_labels (list of ints same length as word_token_indices), token_count (int). It must produce kept_indices (list of ints, indices of tokens whose broadcast label is 1) and token_labels (list of ints of length token_count where each entry is the label broadcast from the word that contains that token). The broadcast: for each word i, assign its label to all token indices in word_token_indices[i]. Must validate no overlap, no out-of-range (0 <= index < token_count), and all token indices from 0 to token_count-1 must be covered exactly once (i.e., union of all word_token_indices must be all tokens). If not, raise ValueError.

Implementation: flatten mapping from token index to label. Use a list of length token_count initialized to None. For each word i, for each token idx in word_token_indices[i]: if already set, raise ValueError (overlap); if out of range, raise ValueError; set token_labels[idx] = word_labels[i]. After processing all words, check if any token_labels entry is None -> uncovered token, raise ValueError. Then compute kept_indices = [i for i, label in enumerate(token_labels) if label == 1]. Return {"kept_indices": kept_indices, "token_labels": token_labels}.

Edge cases: Ensure order of kept_indices is ascending (natural order as we iterate). The "stable_order" property: keep original token order. So we just collect in increasing index order.

Now produce Python code as a JSON string. Must be valid JSON with implementation key.

Also ensure no mutation of case. We'll create a local variable.

Write code with proper error handling.
